judgements.justification: The verbal assessments differ: B's 3 rests on a specific prior-work and time-constant critique that no A reviewer wrote, so the gap is not a calibration gap.
A's reviewers rated well above the accept level (8, 7, 8, 9), so A's oral does not rest on agreement alone at accept-level scores.
A's Reviewer_BSPV raised to 7 on a promised limitations section, and his follow-up question on whether rate coding brings back the lag got no technical answer.

A's one-sentence meta-review cites 'thorough experimental results' and omits BSPV's plausibility caveat, BSPV's 'a bit simplistic' robustness view and ztYa's requested comparisons; B's meta-review carried VGyX's points forward as required revisions.
A's Reviewer_DcW4 gave a 9 partly on the wrong claim that prospective coding 'has no precedence in the literature', which the paper's own Köndgen citation and Brea et al. 2016 contradict.
No rebuttal conceded an unfavourable fact about the results; the concessions on prior work and time constants appear in the camera-ready, and B's scores did not stay high against them.
VGyX's objections were in his initial review and answered in the rebuttal; his post-rebuttal reply drew an author reply of thanks, so the authors had a chance to answer.
The scores and arguments differ (B has a 3 with a specific critique), so the split is not a matter of tier cut-offs on near-identical reviews.
B's area chair did weigh the confident specialist VGyX and made his points required revisions; A's best-informed critic BSPV ended at accept.

A's main concerns (limitations section, Brea citation, wording of the forgetting claim) could be closed in the response and BSPV rose; B's main concern, that faster-than-τm responses were known and need short time constants, no response could fix, and no B score moved.
VGyX's 3 against 9 and 8 pulled B's mean to 6.67; without him B's ratings (9, 8) exceed A's mean of 8.0.
The outlying reviewer VGyX engaged with the rebuttal and replied with further references.
B's area chair did not set VGyX's score aside as unreliable; it adopted his points as required revisions.
Neither committee raised audience breadth or venue fit.
A's meta-review omits reservations but does not misstate the reviewers' final positions, which all ended at accept; B's meta-review reports VGyX's points accurately.
Two of A's four reviewers did not reply, but BSPV revised and ztYa replied; the response did not answer a point that held a score down, so no unrevised score mattered.
B's Reviewer_iVNT gave a 9 at confidence 4 while admitting 'uncertainties in my understanding' of Eq. 2 and Fig. 1, and B's area chair accepted on the 9 and the 8 at full weight.
B's split was two accepts against one reject, not an even split, and A had no split.
The notes show no substantive conflict between the responses; the authors made like concessions to both committees, as the camera-ready reflects.

A's DcW4 accepted a 'no precedence' claim that the paper's own citations contradict, and no A reviewer knew the Knight and van Vreeswijk–Sompolinsky prior work on faster-than-τm responses that B's VGyX cited.
A's oral follows from four accept scores with mean 8.0 and a meta-review that cites the reviewers' agreement on novelty and elegance.
VGyX objected within the paper's own field (theoretical neuroscience) on prior work and time constants, not from a neighbouring field's premises.
A had no critic for a champion to answer, and B's champions did not argue against VGyX (iVNT kept 9 without argument), so the champion asymmetry did not drive the split.
Neither committee rejected the paper because promised revisions were too large; both accepted it.
Both area chairs relied only on the reviews in their records.
Both committees judged the paper as a modelling and learning-theory contribution; neither applied a contribution-type standard the other did not.
VGyX's 3 rests on prior work and synaptic time constants that bear on the headline fast-computation claim, not on a peripheral point; the weak seed complaint was not its basis.
